cluster hypothesis tests are not necessarily good predictors of the relative effectiveness of retrieval using cluster-based ranking and that the correlation between these tests and the relative effectiveness can depend on the size of the list analyzed.

cluster hypothesis tests are negatively correlated with each other, that some tests are also negatively related to the relative effectiveness of the cluster-based retrieval, and that these correlations are affected by the size of the analyzed result list.

the correlation between the effectiveness of cluster- and document-based retrieval, and the extent to which a particular cluster hypothesis test holds, is often low, and in some cases, negative, and that the size of the list of results that is analyzed, as well as the choice of the cluster hypothesis test, can affect the strength of the correlation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cluster hypothesis is a complex concept, which cannot be fully captured by a single test, and which can be affected by various factors.
the extent to which cluster hypothesis tests are correlated with the relative performance of cluster-based retrieval depends on several factors.

, although there is some evidence that cluster hypothesis tests are correlated with the relative efficiency of retrieval using cluster-based representations, this correlation is weak and is affected by several factors.
